12-years-a-slave.plot: Solomon Northup, a free Black violinist, is lured to Washington by two men and wakes to find he has been sold. From that day he is passed from plantation to plantation in Louisiana as a slave.

a-prophet.plot: Malik enters a French prison at nineteen, belonging to no crew. The Corsican gang tells him to kill someone. He does it, and at the same time gathers the relationships inside and outside the prison into his own hands.

a-separation.plot: Nader and Simin are divorcing. Simin wants to take their daughter abroad; Nader will not leave his father, who has dementia. After an accident involving the carer, both families are pulled into the same court case.

a-serious-man.plot: Larry, a university physics teacher, feels everything coming loose: his wife is leaving him for someone else, a student offers money for a passing grade, and an anonymous letter is ruining his tenure. He goes to the rabbis to find out what he did wrong.

adaptation.plot: The screenwriter Charlie takes on a book about an orchid thief and cannot adapt it. As he writes, he writes himself, and his twin brother Donald, into the script.

aftersun.plot: Eleven-year-old Sophie and her father Calum swim, play cards, and watch other people sing at a holiday village in Turkey. Years later, the adult Sophie goes back through the videotapes from that trip.

almost-famous.plot: A rock magazine sends the high-schooler William on the road with a band that is not famous yet. The guitarist, Penny, who follows the band, and the interviews along the way are all messier than he was ready for.

amelie.plot: Amélie waits tables at a café in Montmartre. She likes arranging small good turns for strangers and cannot say what she feels. She returns a tin box from someone’s childhood, and starts to notice a man who keeps coming into the café.

amour.plot: Georges and Anne, retired music teachers, live in a Paris apartment. After a stroke, the right side of Anne’s body fails. Georges keeps the carers, their daughter, and the hospital outside, and looks after her himself.

anatomy-of-a-fall.plot: Samuel is found dead in the snow outside a chalet in the French mountains. His wife Sandra says she was away when it happened. Their son, who does not see well, was inside. The court has to decide whether he fell or was pushed.

anchorman-the-legend-of-ron-burgundy.plot: Ron Burgundy and his crew have the prime-time desk at a San Diego station to themselves. The station sends in the reporter Veronica, and she and Ron compete for the same job.

arrival.plot: Twelve alien ships stop over different places on Earth. The beings inside communicate with ink-like rings of symbols. The linguist Louise is brought in by the military to work out what the symbols mean.

before-sunset.plot: Jesse is signing his last book in a Paris bookshop when Céline appears. He has a few hours before his flight back to the United States. The two of them walk along the Seine and talk.

best-in-show.plot: Several very different people bring their dogs from around the country to Philadelphia for a national dog show. The camera follows them on the road and into their hotels, up to the moment they walk the dogs into the ring.

black-panther.plot: T’Challa returns to Wakanda to take the throne. Erik, in exile, comes back with his father’s grievance to contest the crown, and to put the technology the country has been hiding into other people’s hands.

black-swan.plot: The ballet dancer Nina is competing for both the White Swan and the Black Swan in Swan Lake. The director pushes her to let out the side of herself she cannot control, and she starts seeing another self in the rehearsal room and at home.

borat.plot: Borat, a Kazakh journalist, is sent to the United States to film a documentary about the local culture. He and his producer travel the country, using interviews to push the people they meet into the script he has already prepared.

boyhood.plot: After his parents divorce, Mason moves around Texas with his mother. Stepfathers arrive and leave, his father shows up now and then, and he slowly gets a girlfriend, until he leaves home for college.

bridesmaids.plot: Annie’s cake shop has failed, and so has the relationship she is in. Her friend Lillian is getting married and asks her to be a bridesmaid. Another, wealthy bridesmaid competes with her at every turn.

brokeback-mountain.plot: In 1963 Ennis and Jack are hired to herd sheep in the mountains. When the summer ends they go back to their own lives. For years afterward they meet on the excuse of fishing. Both have wives and children.

call-me-by-your-name.plot: In the summer of 1983, at his family’s house in Italy, Elio meets Oliver, an American graduate student who has come to help Elio’s father with his research. Over a few weeks the two of them move from testing each other to being together. When the summer ends, Oliver goes back to the United States.

carol.plot: In the 1950s the department-store clerk Therese meets Carol at the counter, where Carol has come to buy a gift for her daughter. Carol is in the middle of a divorce that is going against her. The two of them leave together anyway.

children-of-men.plot: No baby has been born in the world for eighteen years. Theo, a former activist, is asked by an old acquaintance to escort a young refugee who has suddenly become pregnant through the checkpoints of Britain.

city-of-god.plot: Rocket wants to be a photographer, not a drug dealer. Li’l Zé, who grew up with him, takes the territory and the guns in a Rio slum into his own hands. The story starts with a few guns changing owners.

crouching-tiger-hidden-dragon.plot: Li Mu Bai asks Yu Shu Lien to take the Green Destiny sword to Sir Te. Jade Fox’s pupil Jen steals it on the way. Shu Lien goes after the sword, Lo waits in the desert for Jen to choose, and Li Mu Bai leaves a great deal unsaid.

eternal-sunshine-of-the-spotless-mind.plot: Joel discovers that his ex-girlfriend Clementine has had him erased from her memory, and goes to have the same procedure. While the deletion is underway, he tries, inside his own mind, to keep her.

everything-everywhere-all-at-once.plot: Evelyn is upstairs from the laundromat, preparing to meet a tax auditor. Her father is visiting from China, and her daughter will not talk to her properly. A husband from another universe tells her she is the only one who can jump into all of her lives.

fish-tank.plot: Fifteen-year-old Mia lives on an Essex estate, cannot stand her mother or her sister, and dances behind a closed door. Her mother’s new boyfriend, Connor, moves in and takes an interest in the dancing.

frances-ha.plot: Frances is studying dance in New York and shares an apartment with her best friend Sophie. After Sophie decides to move out, Frances starts staying short stretches in other people’s homes, and the work dries up.

get-out.plot: Chris goes with his white girlfriend to her family’s place in the country for the weekend. The parents are excessively warm. The gardener and the housekeeper react strangely. At night he is pulled into a gathering he cannot follow.

gladiator.plot: The Roman general Maximus finishes a war and is ordered killed by the new emperor, Commodus. His family is killed too. He survives, is sold as a gladiator, and fights his way back to the arena in Rome.

gone-girl.plot: On their fifth anniversary Amy disappears from the house, and the scene shows signs of a struggle. The police and the press quickly turn their suspicion on her husband Nick, and Nick’s own account becomes harder and harder to stand on.

gravity.plot: On her first spacewalk, the medical engineer Stone is caught in a chain collision of satellite debris, and the craft is destroyed. She and the veteran astronaut Matt are left in orbit and have to find the next ship that still works.

grizzly-man.plot: Every summer Timothy Treadwell lived alone among the grizzlies in Alaska and filmed himself with the bears. In 2003 he and his girlfriend were killed in a bear attack. The film looks back at those summers through the footage he left.

her.plot: Theodore writes letters for other people for a living and has just ended a marriage. He brings home an operating system that can talk. The system names itself Samantha, and the two of them grow closer the more they talk.

in-the-mood-for-love.plot: Chow Mo-wan and Su Li-zhen move, one after the other, into neighboring apartments and discover that their spouses are having an affair. The two of them start meeting often, and stop the conversation before it crosses the line.

inception.plot: Cobb makes his living by entering other people’s dreams and stealing secrets. This time the job is the reverse: to plant an idea in an heir’s mind. He takes a team down into deeper layers of the dream.

inglourious-basterds.plot: In 1944 Lieutenant Aldo leads a unit of Jewish American soldiers hunting Nazis in occupied France. At the same time, the Jewish woman Shosanna is running a cinema that is about to screen a film for the Nazi high command.

inside-llewyn-davis.plot: The folk singer Llewyn is getting through a New York winter. His partner has just killed himself, and his manager will not push his record anymore. He sleeps on friends’ couches and plays one unpaid gig after another.

interstellar.plot: The crops on Earth are dying. Cooper, a former engineer, is recruited to leave the solar system and find the next place humanity can land. When he sets out, his daughter Murph is still a child.

kill-bill-vol-1.plot: The Bride is shot at her wedding rehearsal by her former lover Bill and his assassination squad, and spends four years in a coma. When she wakes she writes a list and starts working back through it, beginning with a sword maker in Okinawa and a house in Tokyo.

lady-bird.plot: Christine renames herself Lady Bird and is determined to leave Sacramento for college on the East Coast. Her mother says the family does not have the money. Applications, a job, and a dance all turn into fights.

let-the-right-one-in.plot: Twelve-year-old Oskar lives in an apartment block in Stockholm and is bullied at school. The new neighbor, Eli, appears only at night, does not feel the cold, and offers to be his friend. People in the same neighborhood start to disappear.

little-miss-sunshine.plot: The Hoover family gets word that their younger daughter Olive has reached the finals of a children’s beauty pageant in California. Grandfather, parents, uncle, and a brother who barely speaks pile into a van that keeps breaking down, and set off to make the contest.

lost-in-translation.plot: Bob, a movie star past his peak, is in Tokyo to shoot a whiskey commercial and cannot sleep. Charlotte is staying in the same hotel with her husband, who is busy with other things. The two of them start spending time in the city together.

mad-max-fury-road.plot: Immortan Joe holds the water and the gasoline in the wasteland. Furiosa steals his wives. Max is strapped to the front of a car, and a whole convoy of war machines chases the tanker.

melancholia.plot: Justine falls apart at her own wedding, and no one can pull her back. Afterward she moves in with her sister Claire. A planet called Melancholia is approaching in the sky. Claire starts to be afraid. Justine stops being afraid.

memento.plot: Lenny’s short-term memory lasts only a few minutes. After his wife is murdered, he keeps investigating with Polaroids, notes, and words tattooed on his body, because he cannot remember what happened a moment ago.

memories-of-murder.plot: In 1986 a series of rape-murders hits a small city in Korea. The local detective Park Doo-man works by instinct and his fists. Seo Tae-yoon, sent from Seoul, insists on evidence. Suspects are brought in one after another, and none of them fit.

michael-clayton.plot: The lawyer Michael is the person his firm sends to clean up trouble. His colleague Arthur, handling a class action against a large company, has a breakdown and denounces the client in public. Michael is sent to make him stop.

minority-report.plot: Washington uses three people who can see murders before they happen, and arrests the killers before the crime. One day John, the chief of Precrime, sees his own name in the system.

moneyball.plot: The Oakland Athletics do not have the money to bid against rich clubs for stars, and still have to build next season’s roster. The general manager Billy Beane stops buying players on a scout’s hunch and starts looking at numbers the market undervalues, such as on-base percentage.

moonlight.plot: A thin boy in Miami grows up around a drug dealer, and as a teenager falls in love with a classmate. As an adult he has a different name and a different body, and waits in a restaurant for that person to appear.

mulholland-drive.plot: Betty comes to Hollywood to be an actress and finds, in the place where she is staying, a woman who has lost her memory in a car crash. The two of them name her Rita and try to find out who she is.

no-country-for-old-men.plot: A veteran finds, in the desert, a sum of money that drug dealers did not have time to take, and decides to take it. A killer with a cattle gun follows the trail. The old sheriff in town watches it go on.

o-brother-where-art-thou.plot: In Mississippi in the 1930s, Everett escapes a prison farm with two companions to find a treasure he says he buried. Along the way they cut a record and get pulled into a governor’s race, and the police stay behind them.

oceans-eleven.plot: Danny Ocean gets out of prison and sets his sights on a vault shared by three casinos. He finds his old partner Rusty and makes up the other nine, each of them responsible for a step Danny cannot get past himself.

oldboy.plot: Oh Dae-su is locked for fifteen years in a room whose location he cannot tell. Television is his only window. The day he is let out, the other side gives him five days to find out who locked him up, and why.

once-upon-a-time-in-hollywood.plot: In 1969 the fading actor Rick Dalton and his stunt double Cliff are looking for the next job in Hollywood. Their neighbor is Roman Polanski. On the same street, a group of young people is taking an interest in that house.

oppenheimer.plot: The physicist Oppenheimer is asked to lead the building of the atomic bomb at Los Alamos. After the bomb is made, the film moves to a hearing years later: his loyalty, his marriage, and whether he can still be trusted with state secrets.

pans-labyrinth.plot: In Spain in 1944, Ofelia follows her mother into a marriage with a brutal officer. In a labyrinth she meets a faun, who gives her three tasks and tells her she is the princess of an underground kingdom.

parasite.plot: The four Kims live in a semi-basement and get by folding pizza boxes. The son forges his credentials and enters the Park household as a tutor. His parents and his sister follow him in, one by one.

past-lives.plot: Nora leaves Seoul with her family as a child and loses touch with her classmate Hae Sung. More than twenty years later she is a writer in New York and already married, and Hae Sung flies in to see her.

phantom-thread.plot: The dressmaker Reynolds Woodcock makes gowns for the famous in London. His sister and a fixed routine run the house. The waitress Alma comes into the workroom as his model, and wants a place of her own in that house.

portrait-of-a-lady-on-fire.plot: The painter Marianne is hired to paint a portrait of Héloïse, who is about to be married, on the condition that Héloïse not know she is being painted. After the daily walks, the arrangement cannot hold.

punch-drunk-love.plot: Barry sells novelty plungers, cannot talk to people, and has seven sisters who call to humiliate him. He is first dragged in by a phone scam, and then meets Lena, who is awkward in the same way.

ratatouille.plot: Remy, a rat with a sharp palate, will not eat garbage anymore. He runs to a once-great restaurant in Paris, climbs into the toque of the apprentice Linguini, and directs this person who cannot cook by pulling his hair.

roma.plot: The maid Cleo works for a middle-class family in Mexico City. The lady of the house has a husband who stays away. Cleo herself becomes pregnant, and the father of the child disappears.

spirited-away.plot: Chihiro and her parents wander into a town of spirits, and her parents are turned into pigs for eating too much. She goes to work for the woman who runs the bathhouse, trying to turn her parents back, and to help Haku remember who he is.

spotlight.plot: The new editor of The Boston Globe tells the investigations team to look at an old lead: Catholic priests abused children, and the church buried it by transferring them. The team starts from a list and knocks on the victims’ doors.

superbad.plot: Seth and Evan are about to finish high school and want to bring alcohol to a classmate’s party, in front of the girls they like. Their friend Fogell gets a fake police ID and is pulled into a shift by two real officers.

tar.plot: The conductor Lydia Tár is at the top of her career, preparing to record Mahler in Berlin. News arrives that a former protégée has died. Her relationships with young people, and her authority in the orchestra, start to come loose together.

the-act-of-killing.plot: Men who took part in the 1965 killings in Indonesia are now local figures of standing. The filmmakers ask them to choose a movie genre and reenact how they killed.

the-dark-knight.plot: The Joker drags Gotham’s gangs and its citizens into his rules, and forces Batman to choose between revealing who he is and keeping the mask. The prosecutor Harvey Dent was the city’s other hope.

the-departed.plot: The gang boss Costello has an informer inside the police, and the state police send a new man into his crew. The two moles are each looking for the other, and each has to keep himself alive first.

the-favourite.plot: Queen Anne is frail and asks little about affairs of state. Her companion Sarah has long made the decisions for her. Sarah’s poor cousin Abigail enters the palace as a maid and soon becomes another person who can get close to the queen.

the-florida-project.plot: Six-year-old Moonee and her friends live in a cheap motel next to Disney World in Orlando, and spend the summer playing between the corridors and the fast-food shops. Her mother Halley makes the rent by letting rooms and by other means.

the-gleaners-and-i.plot: The director drives through the countryside and the cities of France looking for people who pick up what is left. Some take the potatoes a harvester missed, some take vegetables after a market closes, and some turn what they find into work of their own.

the-grand-budapest-hotel.plot: Gustave, the concierge of a mountain hotel, is written into an old guest’s will and is promptly framed for murder. The lobby boy Zero flees with him, and listens to him describe what the hotel used to be.

the-hurt-locker.plot: On the Iraq war’s bomb squads, Sergeant James replaces a predecessor who was killed and leads a three-man team. His sense of the danger is not the same as the other two men’s. When he rotates home, he does not know what else he can do.

the-lives-of-others.plot: In East Berlin in 1984, the Stasi captain Wiesler is ordered to listen in on the playwright Dreyman and his girlfriend. The surveillance goes on for a long time. What he writes in his reports starts to differ from what he hears in the headphones.

the-lord-of-the-rings-the-fellowship-of-.plot: Frodo receives a ring from Bilbo, and Gandalf tells him the ring has to be destroyed. He and his companions leave the Shire, meet the others at Rivendell, and the Fellowship sets out for Mordor.

the-master.plot: The veteran Freddie gets by on liquor he brews himself, and is picked out on a boat by Lancaster Dodd. Dodd leads an organization called the Cause and keeps Freddie beside him, as a subject and as a follower.

the-royal-tenenbaums.plot: The three Tenenbaum children were prodigies and, as adults, have each stalled. Their father Royal, who has ignored the family for years, claims he is dying and moves back in.

the-social-network.plot: The Harvard student Zuckerberg writes, in one night, a site that rates his classmates, and then builds what becomes Facebook with his roommates. After the company grows, he ends up in court against a co-founder and against an early investor.

the-tree-of-life.plot: Jack remembers a childhood in Texas: a severe father, a gentle mother, and the death of his brother. Those scenes from the house are set between images of the universe forming and of life appearing.

the-wolf-of-wall-street.plot: The stockbroker Jordan Belfort opens his own firm and makes money by talking clients into buying junk stocks. Money and drugs pull the whole office upward, and a federal investigation follows.

the-worst-person-in-the-world.plot: Julie is thirty. She leaves medical school halfway through for psychology, and later wants to take photographs. She leaves the boyfriend she lives with, meets someone else in a bar, and finds she still cannot settle.

the-zone-of-interest.plot: Rudolf Höss is the commandant of Auschwitz. The film stays with his wife and children in the villa outside the wall: planting flowers, having guests, choosing clothes sent over from the camp.

there-will-be-blood.plot: Daniel Plainview starts from a single oil well and buys up the land around it. Eli, a young local preacher, wants a share of the money, and wants Daniel to confess in public.

toni-erdmann.plot: Ines, a corporate consultant, is in Romania helping a client cut staff. Her father decides she no longer knows him, puts in false teeth, and turns up among her clients as a life coach.

uncut-gems.plot: The jeweler Howard keeps a black opal in the shop, owes a loan shark, and has his money on a Celtics game. Each new sum is used to plug the hole left by the last one.

under-the-skin.plot: A being in the shape of a woman drives a van along the roads of Scotland, asks men who are alone for directions, and takes them into the van. The people who are taken do not appear again. She repeats this until she starts to leave the route.

up.plot: After his wife Ellie dies, the balloon salesman Carl lifts the house with thousands of balloons and flies toward South America, as the two of them agreed when they were young. The scout Russell is left on the porch by accident.

volver.plot: Raimunda goes back to her hometown to see her aunt and finds her mother’s ghost in the town. What she brings back to Madrid is not only that, but a body in her sister’s house that has to be dealt with.

wall-e.plot: The trash robot WALL-E packs garbage day after day on an abandoned Earth. The probe EVE lands to take a sample. He follows her off the planet, onto a ship carrying what is left of humanity.

whiplash.plot: The drummer Andrew gets into a conservatory and is picked by the teacher Fletcher for the core band. Fletcher uses insults and cuts to make him play faster, and Andrew starts moving everything else out of the way.

y-tu-mama-tambien.plot: Tenoch and Julio claim to know a secret beach and talk the married Luisa into coming with them. The three of them drive toward the sea, and the talk in the car crosses a line a little further each time.

yi-yi.plot: Jian’s mother is in a coma. His company is in the middle of a deal he is not sure of, and a first love appears from Japan. His son Yang-Yang photographs the backs of people’s heads. His daughter is in a romance she is keeping from the family.

zodiac.plot: In the late 1960s a man calling himself the Zodiac sends ciphers and claims of murder to the San Francisco papers. The cartoonist Robert puts the cartoons aside and spends years checking suspects.

30-rock.plot: Liz Lemon runs a Saturday-night comedy show. Her boss, Jack Donaghy, treats management and dating as acquisitions. Every week the actors, the writers, and the network drag the show back from collapse.
30-rock.hook: Tina Fey based it on her years as head writer of Saturday Night Live, and it is about the chaos behind a comedy show. The jokes are packed tight, and the background is full of them too. Alec Baldwin’s network executive, Jack, is the best thing in it.

adolescence.plot: Thirteen-year-old Jamie is arrested at home, accused of killing a classmate. The four episodes follow the arrest, the school, a psychological evaluation, and the aftermath for the family. Each episode is one uninterrupted shot.
adolescence.hook: Each episode is a single take. Four episodes cover four moments after a 13-year-old boy is charged with murder. It is about how online misogyny reaches teenagers, and why the parents and the school did not see it. Owen Cooper, acting for the first time, is especially startling in the third episode, opposite the psychologist.

andor.plot: Before Rogue One, Cassian Andor is not yet a rebel hero. He is pulled into a theft, a prison, and a revolution that runs on ledgers, speeches, and sacrifice.
andor.hook: A Star Wars series that barely relies on Jedi or the Force. It is about ordinary people being pushed into resistance. The politics, the prison, and the spycraft are written for adults, and you can follow it without the other films. The prison stretch of the first season is the high point. The end of the second season runs straight into Rogue One.

anthony-bourdain-no-reservations.plot: An earlier travel-and-food series. Bourdain moves from the kitchen out into the world and records how a place eats, with appetite, jokes, and questions that get more serious as he goes.
anthony-bourdain-no-reservations.hook: Bourdain’s earlier travel-and-food series, looser and more playful than Parts Unknown: street stalls, complaints, drinks, and talk with local people. In 2006 the crew was filming in Lebanon when the war started and they were stuck in Beirut. That episode is a thing apart.

anthony-bourdain-parts-unknown.plot: Bourdain goes places to eat, and spends more of the time sitting down to hear about politics, war, and a day’s work. The food is the reason for being let in, not a way of avoiding the place.
anthony-bourdain-parts-unknown.hook: Anthony Bourdain travels the world to eat, but he is more interested in the people, the politics, and the history behind the food. It is not a checklist of restaurants. It often films war, poverty, and migration. The Vietnam episode, in which he eats bun cha in Hanoi with Obama, is the famous one.

arrested-development.plot: After the developer George Bluth is arrested, his son Michael tries to hold together a family that keeps turning on itself. The narrator supplies the half of the sentence they will not admit, and the jokes are often paid off several episodes later.
arrested-development.hook: After the rich father is arrested, only the second son, Michael, tries to keep the family standing. Everyone else makes it worse. It is one of the comedies you have to watch closely: setups come back episodes, or seasons, later. The first three seasons are the classic run. The fourth and fifth, revived by Netflix, were received less well.

atlanta.plot: Earn drops out and comes back to Atlanta to manage the early career of his cousin, the rapper Paper Boi. The city, race, and fame do not behave as expected here, and some episodes simply walk into another genre.
atlanta.hook: On the surface, a broke young man manages his cousin, a rapper. In practice each episode can be a different kind of show: sometimes an absurd comedy, sometimes something like a horror film. It writes Black life in America in its own way, without lectures, and it keeps pricking. The second-season episode “Teddy Perkins” is the one people single out.

baby-reindeer.plot: Donny, a comedian working in a bar, offers a kindness to a woman at the bar, and she begins stalking him for a long time. The story then turns to the abuse Donny has hidden for years, and to why he did not cut the relationship off at once.
baby-reindeer.hook: Based on Richard Gadd’s own experience: a struggling comedian is stalked by a woman. The first half plays like a thriller. The second half uncovers the sexual abuse in his past, and it is very heavy. The performances feel real. Jessica Gunning’s stalker stays with you.

band-of-brothers.plot: Following Stephen Ambrose’s account, it stays with Easy Company of the 101st Airborne, from training camp in Georgia to Normandy, the Ardennes, and Hitler’s Eagle’s Nest. The company gets to know itself again as the numbers drop.
band-of-brothers.hook: Produced by Hanks and Spielberg, it follows Easy Company of the 101st Airborne from training through the end of the Second World War. Each episode opens with interviews with the real veterans. The fighting is plain and brutal. “Bastogne” and “Why We Fight” are the episodes people remember.

barry.plot: The hit man Barry Berkman comes to Los Angeles for a job, wanders into an acting class, and decides he might become an actor. The work of killing and the wish to be seen start competing for the same calendar.
barry.hook: A hit man comes to Los Angeles for a job, stumbles into an acting class, and tries to switch careers. It starts as a black comedy and gets darker, closer to a crime tragedy. Bill Hader stars and directs. The second-season episode “ronny/lily” is the famous one.

battlestar-galactica.plot: The Cylon robots nearly wipe out humanity. What is left of the fleet, under Commander Adama and President Roslin, searches for a legendary Earth. The enemy looks human, and can love, and can believe.
battlestar-galactica.hook: The Cylons nearly destroy humanity, and the survivors flee with a warship. It looks like space science fiction and is really about war, religion, democracy, and terrorism. A lot of it clearly shadows the United States after September 11. The first two seasons are the strongest.

beef.plot: The contractor Danny and the shop owner Amy honk at each other in a parking lot, and a bout of road rage turns into the wrecking of each other’s lives. Both of them are barely holding up a self that still looks all right.
beef.hook: Two strangers get into a road-rage fight in a parking lot, and the revenge keeps escalating. The black humor is strong. Under it are Asian families, class anxiety, and loneliness. Steven Yeun and Ali Wong are very good in it. Ten episodes, tightly paced, and eight Emmys.

better-call-saul.plot: Jimmy McGill is a slippery lawyer. His brother Chuck looks down on him, and his girlfriend Kim knows where the line is better than he does. To become Saul Goodman he renames himself, changes his trade, and changes himself, a piece at a time.
better-call-saul.hook: A prequel to Breaking Bad, about how Jimmy becomes Saul Goodman. It is slower than the original, and the people are drawn more finely. Rhea Seehorn’s Kim is one of the best roles in the show. You can watch it without Breaking Bad. If you have seen Breaking Bad, it hurts more.

better-things.plot: Sam, an actress in Los Angeles, raises three daughters on her own, takes jobs, looks after her mother, and keeps her own days going in an industry that does not treat her as the lead. The plot is loose. A day is a day.
better-things.hook: Sam, a single mother and an actress, is raising three daughters in Los Angeles and looking after her mother across the street. The episodes are ordinary life: arguments, cooking, driving, and they feel true. It suits people who want a woman’s point of view and stories about family.

black-mirror.plot: Each episode is a near future: memory can be replayed, social life can be scored, a mind can be copied into another body. The technology is rarely the only villain. The desire to use it is.
black-mirror.hook: An anthology. Each episode is a near-future technology story: social scores, memory playback, uploading a mind. The technology magnifies a weakness in people. You do not have to watch in order. Start with the well-liked ones: “San Junipero,” “White Bear,” and “Nosedive.” The first three seasons are the steadiest.

bojack-horseman.plot: BoJack, a washed-up horse star, lives in Hollywood on alcohol, self-pity, and the reruns of an old sitcom. The city where animals and people live together is funny, until the damage he causes can no longer be covered by a joke.
bojack-horseman.hook: It looks like an absurd cartoon about animals. It is about depression, addiction, childhood damage, and a celebrity destroying himself. The first half of a season is often the jokes. The second half can turn heavy without warning. The almost wordless underwater episode in season three, and the eulogy episode in season five, are the ones people come back to.

breaking-bad.plot: Walter White, a high-school chemistry teacher, is diagnosed with lung cancer. To leave money for his family he partners with his former student Jesse and starts making meth. A living made in a trailer slowly becomes an empire he will not hand over.
breaking-bad.hook: You watch an ordinary man become a drug lord, and each turn has a cause. He does not simply go bad. Cranston won four Emmys for best actor in a drama for the role. The first two seasons are a little slow, and it tightens after that. “Ozymandias,” in the fifth season, is often called one of the best single episodes in American television.

broad-city.plot: Abbi and Ilana work, get lost, and help each other in New York, and keep pulling each other into worse ideas. The friendship is not the background. It is the thing each episode has to get done.
broad-city.hook: Two women in New York have no money and no career. They wander the city, get into trouble, and compliment each other. It is one of the few comedies built on a friendship between women, and it does not move forward on a romance. It grew out of web shorts. The style is loose, and it is easy to watch while you eat.

catastrophe.plot: Sharon, from Ireland, and Rob, from the United States, have a short relationship in London, and then an unplanned pregnancy. They decide to keep the child and try to turn the politeness of strangers into a marriage.
catastrophe.hook: An American man and an Irish woman have a one-night stand in London, she gets pregnant, and they decide to stay together. It is a very adult romantic comedy: the dialogue is crude, honest, and funny. Episodes run about 25 minutes. The marriage and the child-rearing feel real.

chappelles-show.plot: Chappelle uses sketches and talk with the studio audience to take apart race, celebrity, and the false propriety of television. Many of the bits were quoted for years afterward, and became part of the break between him and the show.
chappelles-show.hook: Dave Chappelle’s sketch show, which handles race, celebrity, and pop culture directly. Bits such as “Rick James” are still quoted. At the height of the show, Chappelle walked away, and that departure was argued over at length. Only two seasons were completed.

chernobyl.plot: In 1986 the Chernobyl nuclear plant explodes. The scientist Legasov, the official Shcherbina, and the nuclear physicist Khomyuk have to stop a disaster that is not finished, after the lie has already gone out.
chernobyl.hook: A five-episode miniseries of the 1986 nuclear accident, from the night of the explosion through the hearings afterward. What is most frightening is not the images of radiation. It is how the bureaucracy covered up what had happened. The atmosphere is oppressive, the detail is careful, and the Douban score sits above 9.

community.plot: Jeff Winger, disbarred, enrolls at a community college and assembles a study group that takes every class together. The show will spend a whole episode as another genre: an action movie, a documentary, an 8-bit game.
community.hook: A group of people with nothing in common form a study group at a community college. Whole episodes parody a genre: paintball, a gangster film, a documentary. Seasons two and three are the strongest. The creator was later fired and then brought back, and the quality swings.

curb-your-enthusiasm.plot: Larry David plays a television writer with his own name, and in Los Angeles turns every small thing — a tip, a funeral, a hello — into a social disaster. The outline is set. The dialogue is often improvised.
curb-your-enthusiasm.hook: Larry David, the creator of Seinfeld, plays a version of himself and specializes in turning small questions into disasters: whether to tip, whether you can take another sample. There is no full script, only an outline, and a lot of the dialogue is improvised, so the embarrassment feels real. Episodes mostly stand alone. You can start anywhere.

deadwood.plot: In the 1870s the town of Deadwood, in the Dakota Territory, has no formal law yet. The gold, the saloons, and the brothels arrive first. Sheriff Seth Bullock and the saloon owner Al Swearengen negotiate who runs the town.
deadwood.hook: A gold-rush town in 1870s South Dakota has no law. Order is built, a piece at a time, by a saloon owner and a sheriff. The dialogue is half classical and half obscenity, like a western written by Shakespeare. Ian McShane’s Al is the soul of the show. It was cancelled after three seasons. A film in 2019 closed it.

dexter.plot: Dexter, a blood-spatter analyst for the Miami police, follows a code his adoptive father left him and kills only murderers who got away. By day he learns how to be an ordinary person. At night he packs the other life into freezer bags.
dexter.hook: Dexter, a blood-spatter analyst for the Miami police, is privately a serial killer who only kills people he judges guilty. The first four seasons are the best. The Trinity Killer, in season four, is the peak. The later seasons drop off, and the original ending was badly received.

downton-abbey.plot: After 1912, on an estate in Yorkshire, the Crawley family and the servants downstairs are tied to the same house. Inheritance, war, and a rising middle class slowly change the rules above and below stairs.
downton-abbey.hook: An English aristocratic house at the start of the twentieth century. Upstairs is the Earl of Grantham’s family. Downstairs are the servants. It plays like a high-end family soap. The clothes, the manners, and the change of the era are all good to look at. Maggie Smith’s dowager has a line worth keeping almost every time she speaks.

eastbound-and-down.plot: Kenny Powers, a baseball pitcher past his prime, comes home and teaches phys ed at the middle school, while remaining sure he is still a star. Obscenity, drugs, and a comeback that does not exist are how he arranges his life.
eastbound-and-down.hook: Kenny Powers, a washed-up baseball star, comes home to teach phys ed. He is vain, rude, and foul-mouthed. The jokes are low, and they are also a satire of an American idea of manhood. Danny McBride plays him without holding back.

enlightened.plot: After Amy Jellicoe breaks down at her company, she goes on a retreat and comes back determined to be a better person, and to blow the whistle on the company that hurt her. Her goodwill is often real. Her methods are often a disaster.
enlightened.hook: Laura Dern plays a woman who has a breakdown and comes back from a retreat “enlightened.” At the company she tries to be good and to expose it, and keeps making the room unbearable. The creator, Mike White, later made The White Lotus. Two seasons, highly regarded, and not widely known.

fleabag.plot: A woman running a café in London talks to the camera to get away from her family, her customers, and her own grief. In the second season she meets a priest who is not supposed to cross the line either.
fleabag.hook: The heroine keeps complaining to the camera. You laugh first, and later realize she is using the jokes to stay away from grief. Two seasons, twelve episodes, an afternoon. The second season adds Andrew Scott’s priest. It won the 2019 Emmys for comedy series, lead actress, writing, and directing.

friday-night-lights.plot: The town of Dillon, Texas, measures almost everything by Friday-night high-school football. The coach Eric Taylor and his wife Tami make the week’s decisions between winning, the children’s futures, and their own marriage.
friday-night-lights.hook: The setting is a high-school football team in a Texas town, and you can watch it without knowing the sport. The point is the people in the town. The coach’s marriage is often called one of the most believable marriages on American television. A lot of handheld camera and improvisation makes the people feel unusually natural.

game-of-thrones.plot: Several houses in Westeros contest the Iron Throne. Beyond the Wall in the north, a winter that most people treat as legend is also coming. Adapted from the novels of George R. R. Martin, the nobles’ marriages and the battles run on the same set of rules.
game-of-thrones.hook: Under the fantasy is a show about power. Lead characters can die at any time, and no one is safe. That is what made the early seasons grip. The scale of the production is close to a film. “Blackwater” and “The Battle of the Bastards” set a standard for war on television. The last season’s reputation collapsed. The first six are still worth watching.

gilmore-girls.plot: Lorelai had Rory at sixteen, and the two of them grew up in Stars Hollow more like friends. Fast talk, coffee, and an application to the Ivy League keep pulling them back to the richer, stricter family in Hartford.
gilmore-girls.hook: Lorelai, a single mother, and her daughter Rory live in a small town in Connecticut, more like friends than like mother and daughter. The dialogue is extremely fast, the pop-culture references are dense, and the townspeople are each a pleasure. It is very easy to feel better while watching it.

girls.plot: Hannah Horvath wants to be a writer in Brooklyn, and gets through her twenties on her parents’ money, unsteady work, and three friends. Intimacy here is often embarrassing, and it is not going to be written as inspiration.
girls.hook: Four women in their twenties get by in New York: jobs, relationships, and irritation with each other. It does not make young women look glossy. The heroine is selfish and embarrassing, which is why it feels true. A lot of viewers met Adam Driver here for the first time.

hacks.plot: Deborah Vance, a long-running comic in Las Vegas, is slipping, and is forced to work with Ava, a young writer the industry has pushed out. They look down on each other, and each of them needs the other’s sentences.
hacks.hook: An established woman comic in Las Vegas writes material with a young writer the industry has blacklisted. They cannot stand each other at first, and later become the people who understand each other best. Jean Smart has won the Emmy for lead actress in a comedy more than once for it, and the third season also won best comedy series.

halt-and-catch-fire.plot: In the 1980s a salesman, an engineer, and two women who come up from behind go from cloning a personal computer to the early internet. The companies come apart. The people sit down at the same table again because of the same idea.
halt-and-catch-fire.hook: The rise of the personal computer and the internet in the United States from the 1980s into the 1990s. The first season is like a workplace show. Later it becomes a story about four people, their ambitions, working together, and failing. The last two seasons are especially well regarded. It is often called one of the most underrated American series.

happy-valley.plot: Catherine Cawood, a police officer in Yorkshire, is responsible for a valley that is not happy. Tommy Lee Royce, who caused her daughter’s death, is about to get out of prison. The grandson she is raising is the child that violence left behind.
happy-valley.hook: While investigating a kidnapping, the Yorkshire officer Catherine finds that the suspect is the man who assaulted her daughter and led to her daughter’s suicide. The crime plot is tight, and the relationships hurt. Sarah Lancashire’s middle-aged officer is hard, tired, and funny. Three seasons, eighteen episodes.

homeland.plot: The CIA officer Carrie Mathison becomes convinced that Brody, a Marine who has been brought home, has turned. Her judgment is extremely sharp, and it is also steered by bipolar disorder. No one at the agency is willing to believe her completely.
homeland.hook: A Marine comes home after years in captivity, and the CIA officer Carrie suspects he has been turned. The first season holds the question “is he or isn’t he” very well. Claire Danes’s Carrie has a near-genius judgment and is also living with bipolar disorder. She is the center of the show.

house.plot: Gregory House runs a department of diagnostics and takes the cases other doctors have given up. He is sure the patient is lying. He himself stays upright on painkillers, for an injured leg and a worse temper.
house.hook: House is a brilliant doctor, rude, mean, and addicted to painkillers. He diagnoses the cases no one else can solve, and each episode is a detective story in a hospital. Hugh Laurie is British, and the American accent has no cracks in it.

house-of-cards.plot: Frank Underwood, the party whip in Congress, does not get the job he was promised, and starts removing the people in his way, one by one. Now and then he turns to the audience and explains the next step. His wife Claire runs a colder kind of politics.
house-of-cards.hook: The congressman Frank Underwood is passed over for secretary of state and starts scheming his way up. He often speaks straight to the camera. It was Netflix’s first original series that really mattered. The first two seasons are the tightest. Kevin Spacey was dropped after the scandal, and the last season is without him.

how-to-with-john-wilson.plot: Each episode starts from a subject in ordinary life, such as how to make small talk or how to throw out batteries. Wilson walks the streets of New York with a camera, and the voice-over soon leaves the tutorial and meets actual people.
how-to-with-john-wilson.hook: Each episode looks like a how-to: how to make small talk, how to find a parking space. What John Wilson films of the New York street then runs off in another direction. A muttered narration over footage grabbed in the street is often funny and, unexpectedly, moving. It does not rely on written jokes. It relies on looking and on the edit.

i-may-destroy-you.plot: The writer Arabella is drugged and assaulted one night, and afterward has to put that night back together from fragments. Friends, dates, and the work can no longer be explained in the old way.
i-may-destroy-you.hook: Michaela Coel made it from her own sexual assault. She wrote it, stars in it, and directed some of it. The subject is heavy, and the script does not follow a victim template: there is humor, a complicated friendship, and moral questions that stay unclear. Twelve episodes. It stays with you. Coel won the Emmy for writing.

i-think-you-should-leave.plot: Each sketch starts from an ordinary thing: a meeting, a hat, a dinner. Then someone refuses to stop, and the social situation slides out of the normal world according to his logic.
i-think-you-should-leave.hook: Tim Robinson’s sketch show. Each bit starts in an ordinary social situation, and then someone will not admit they are wrong, and it gets further out of hand. The jokes are very strange. If you are on its wavelength, you will lose it. Episodes run under 20 minutes, and the pace is fast.

insecure.plot: Issa works at a nonprofit in Los Angeles and, with her best friend Molly, deals with dating, work, and the sentence that will be regretted the moment it is said. South Los Angeles is not a backdrop. It is the road they drive back and forth.
insecure.hook: Issa Rae on the dating, the work, and the friendships of Black women in Los Angeles. What is best in it is not the romance. It is the friendship between Issa and Molly, who depend on each other and fight often. The music is excellent. Five seasons, and it ends.

its-always-sunny-in-philadelphia.plot: Five people running a bar in Philadelphia are selfish, shortsighted, and sincerely believe they are the most put-upon person in the room. Every episode’s plan fails because of who they are.
its-always-sunny-in-philadelphia.hook: Five selfish, stupid people run an Irish bar in Philadelphia. Each episode they think up a bad idea and then fail completely. They almost never grow up, which is the joke. It has run more than sixteen seasons, the longest-running live-action sitcom on American television.

justified.plot: The federal marshal Raylan Givens is sent back to his home in Kentucky for shooting too quickly. He has to deal not only with the local criminals but with Boyd Crowder, who grew up with him and now preaches and sells drugs.
justified.hook: Adapted from Elmore Leonard. The federal marshal Raylan comes home to Kentucky to enforce the law. He is calm, funny, and very fast with a gun. His opposite, Boyd, can talk. The Southern crime atmosphere is thick, the dialogue has a flavor, and the last season’s ending is a classic.

key-and-peele.plot: Key and Peele use sketches to handle race, pop culture, and the social moments that go wrong as soon as someone speaks. The two of them take turns playing both sides of a power relationship. The joke sits in the instant an identity is misread.
key-and-peele.hook: A sketch show by two comedians. Each bit is a few minutes, easy to watch in pieces. A lot of the sketches are about race and identity, such as Obama and Luther, his “anger translator.” Jordan Peele later directed Get Out.

lost.plot: A passenger plane crashes on a tropical island, and the survivors soon find it is not an ordinary deserted island. Each episode opens someone’s past in flashback. The mysteries on the island keep multiplying.
lost.hook: A plane crashes on a mysterious island, and the survivors meet stranger and stranger things. Each episode cuts in someone’s past. The people are solidly built, and the show started the fashion for mystery series that keep burying clues. The early seasons are extremely addictive. The ending was heavily argued over.

louie.plot: The stand-up comic Louie is raising two daughters in New York. Each episode is like a short film on its own: a failed date, a set, or a small thing that suddenly becomes frightening.
louie.hook: Louis C.K. writes, directs, and stars. Each episode is like a short: sometimes funny, sometimes sad, sometimes absurd. It influenced a lot of later author-driven comedy. He later stopped working after sexual-harassment allegations, and some viewers will not watch it for that reason.

mad-men.plot: On Madison Avenue in the 1960s, the creative director Don Draper invents desires for clients and lives under a name he stole. Gender, drink, and promotion in the office are busier than the advertising.
mad-men.hook: New York advertising in the 1960s. The suits, the cigarettes, the drinks, and the office politics are all made with great care. The main line is the mystery of Don Draper’s identity. Peggy’s rise from secretary to copywriter is just as good to watch, and a decade of social change sits in the background. It is slow, and it rewards attention. It won the Emmy for best drama four years running.

mare-of-easttown.plot: Mare Sheehan, a detective in a small Pennsylvania town, investigates the death of a young mother while dealing with a divorce, the loss of her son, and custody of her grandson. She knows every suspect, because they are neighbors.
mare-of-easttown.hook: A small-town detective investigates the murder of a young mother, and at the same time faces a divorce, her son’s suicide, and custody of her grandson. The mystery is solid. The family scenes are more moving. Kate Winslet won the Emmy for lead actress in a limited series. Seven episodes, and a lot of turns at the end.

modern-family.plot: Three branches of the Pritchett family get through their days in the same city, shot as a fake documentary: a second marriage, a same-sex couple, and a conventional suburban family. The trouble all arrives before dinner.
modern-family.hook: A mockumentary of three related households: an older man with a younger wife, a same-sex couple, and an ordinary family of three. Half an hour an episode, the jokes are steady, and it is easy to watch together. It won the Emmy for best comedy five years in a row.

nathan-for-you.plot: Fielder walks into real small businesses as a consultant and proposes schemes that are excessive and seem as if they might work: fake discounts, a fake romance, a whole procedure designed to confuse the customer. The owners often go along.
nathan-for-you.hook: Nathan Fielder poses as a business consultant and gives real small-business owners absurd ideas, such as a “Dumb Starbucks.” The owners actually try them. The jokes come from the embarrassment and from people’s politeness. As it goes on it becomes more like an experiment about reality and performance. The last episode, “Finding Frances,” is a thing apart.

normal-people.plot: In a school in Sligo, Connell and Marianne are together in secret. At Trinity College in Dublin, class and the way of speaking trade places. They keep separating, and meeting again in the silence the other person knows best.
normal-people.hook: Adapted from Sally Rooney’s novel. Two young people in Ireland come together and apart from secondary school through university. It does not run on big events. It runs on misunderstandings, silence, and class, and that is what makes it hurt. Paul Mescal became known for it. The sex is filmed plainly and with restraint.

ozark.plot: The financial adviser Marty Byrde fails at laundering money for a Mexican cartel and takes his family to the Lake of the Ozarks, using local businesses to clean the money. His wife Wendy soon wants to be more than the cover.
ozark.hook: A financial adviser’s family is forced to flee to a lake district in Missouri and launder money for a Mexican cartel. It is colder than Breaking Bad, and more like a family trying to survive. Julia Garner’s local girl Ruth is the highlight, and she won three Emmys for it.

parks-and-recreation.plot: Leslie Knope works for the parks department in Pawnee, Indiana, and believes that meetings, forms, and a larger breakfast can improve public life. Her colleagues mostly do not believe it, and follow her anyway.
parks-and-recreation.hook: Leslie, in a small-town parks department, genuinely wants to do something for the community. The colleagues around her are each stranger than the last. The first season is fairly close to a copy of The Office. From the second season it becomes warm and funny. Nick Offerman’s Ron Swanson is a classic role.

peaky-blinders.plot: After the First World War, Tommy Shelby takes his family gang in Birmingham up from horse races and street business, and along the way meets the IRA, politicians, and fascists. The razor gang is trying to become a legitimate power.
peaky-blinders.hook: Birmingham after the First World War. The Shelby family fights its way from a street gang into politics. The slow motion, the rock score, and the overcoats and flat caps are all very styled. Cillian Murphy’s Tommy is calm and carrying the war. The first three seasons are the best.

peep-show.plot: Mark and Jeremy share a flat in south London. The camera goes in through their eyes, and the narration says what they are actually thinking: one is an anxious loan manager, the other a musician who will not get a job.
peep-show.hook: A British sitcom. A lot of it is shot from a first-person view, with the two men’s interior monologue, so you hear what they say and what they actually think. One is anxious and prim. The other is lazy and unreliable. They cannot stand each other and cannot leave. One of the writers, Jesse Armstrong, later created Succession.

pen15.plot: Two adult actresses play themselves in the year 2000 and go back to middle school: instant messaging, clothes that do not fit, and a friendship taken seriously to the point of being ridiculous. The classmates around them are played by actual adolescents.
pen15.hook: Two actresses in their thirties play themselves at 13. The classmates are played by actual 13-year-olds. It is middle school around 2000: the embarrassment, the crushes, the friendship, and the various first times. Very funny, and honest.

planet-earth.plot: The BBC’s eleven-part nature series, from the poles, caves, and plains to the deep ocean, records animal behavior that the cameras of the time could barely get near. Attenborough’s narration treats the landscape as a system that is still running.
planet-earth.hook: A BBC nature documentary, filmed over five years, using high-definition cameras on snow leopards, deep-sea life, and the great migrations, images that were rarely seen. David Attenborough’s narration is steady and good to listen to. It set the visual standard for modern nature documentaries. It is best on a large screen.

reservation-dogs.plot: Four Indigenous teenagers on a reservation in Oklahoma plan to leave for California. A friend’s death turns the leaving into an unfinished wish, and the elders in the community keep pulling them back into the specifics of a life.
reservation-dogs.hook: Four Indigenous teenagers on a reservation in Oklahoma steal to save money. They want to go to California and finish a dead friend’s wish. The writers, directors, and principal cast are almost all Indigenous. The humor has a little of the supernatural in it. Three seasons, and it ends. It gets more moving as it goes.

rupauls-drag-race.plot: Drag queens compete in costume, performance, and talking to camera. The loser lip-syncs for the chance to stay. Friendships, competition, and a single remark backstage make the plot of each season.
rupauls-drag-race.hook: A reality competition for drag queens: costume, performance, comedy, and lip-sync. It brought drag into the mainstream, and made a lot of contestants and catchphrases. The sharp judging and the backstage gossip are both good to watch.

scandal.plot: Olivia Pope handles crises in Washington that cannot appear in the papers, and is herself in a relationship with the president that could bring down the White House. Her team is called the gladiators. The job is to rewrite the facts before the deadline.
scandal.hook: Olivia Pope, a crisis manager in Washington, cleans up scandals for the powerful, and is having an affair with the president. The plot turns extremely fast. Almost every episode has something astonishing. It is a political soap with a very satisfying pace. Kerry Washington was the first Black woman in nearly forty years to lead an American network series.

schitts-creek.plot: The Rose family loses its fortune and has to move to the small town they once bought as a joke. In two rooms at the motel, the old manner collides, a little at a time, with the town’s goodwill.
schitts-creek.hook: A rich family goes broke and has to move to a town they bought as a joke. The first season looks like an ordinary comedy about the rich brought low. Later it gets warmer, and each person changes. The last season swept all seven major comedy Emmys.

severance.plot: Employees of Lumon accept a procedure that splits work memory from life memory. After the elevator goes down, another self starts the shift, and does not want to stay in the building forever.
severance.hook: A company’s employees undergo a procedure that separates the memory of work from the memory of life. The self at work does not know who the self at home is. The premise is new, and the retro, cold-colored office design is immediately recognizable. The mysteries stack up. The end of the first season grabs you. Ben Stiller directed most of the first season.

shogun.plot: In Japan in 1600, the English sailor Blackthorne’s ship drifts ashore on the eve of the lords deciding who will rule. Lady Mariko, the translator, carries both languages and both loyalties.
shogun.hook: Japan in 1600, at the end of the warring states. An English navigator washes ashore and is pulled into the struggle among the lords. Most of the dialogue is in Japanese. The costume, the etiquette, and the political maneuvering are all careful. Hiroyuki Sanada stars and produces. The first season won a record 18 Emmys.

six-feet-under.plot: The Fisher family runs a funeral home in Los Angeles. Each episode opens with a death. The living go on arguing, loving, and wheeling the body into the room.
six-feet-under.hook: A family runs a funeral home. Someone dies at the start of each episode, and death becomes an ordinary subject. What it is really about is how the living face loss, sexuality, and the family. The montage in the last few minutes is widely taken as one of the best endings in the history of television.

slow-horses.plot: MI5 posts the agents who have made mistakes to Slough House, under Jackson Lamb, a slovenly old man from the Cold War. The people called the slow horses still run into the cases the head office does not want to handle itself.
slow-horses.hook: MI5 exiles the agents who have failed to Slough House, and this group of losers keeps getting pulled into real cases. Gary Oldman’s boss, Jackson Lamb, is slovenly, vicious, and extremely capable. He alone is worth it. Six episodes a season, fast, easy to watch in one sitting.

somebody-somewhere.plot: After her sister dies, Sam stays in her hometown in Kansas and feels like an outsider there. A choir and her friend Joel get her singing again, and get her learning how to stay in a small town.
somebody-somewhere.hook: Sam, a middle-aged woman, stays in her Kansas hometown after her sister’s death and cannot find a place she belongs, until she joins a singing group of the town’s outsiders. It is slow, with no big reversal, and it is very gentle about friendship and loneliness. The passages where Bridget Everett sings are moving.

squid-game.plot: A group of people in debt agree to play a set of children’s games. The winner takes a huge prize. The losers die on the field. Seong Gi-hun thinks he can still understand the rules through kindness. The rules only count the numbers.
squid-game.hook: 456 people deep in debt play children’s games. Lose and you die. The winner takes a huge sum. The premise is simple and the images are bright. The first season became the most-watched series in Netflix’s history. What actually moves you is the position each player has been pushed into by ordinary life.

station-eleven.plot: After a flu, a traveling symphony walks among the ruins around the Great Lakes and trades Shakespeare for food and a bed. A comic book joins several strangers from the night of the outbreak, twenty years later.
station-eleven.hook: Twenty years after a lethal flu destroys civilization, a traveling troupe performs Shakespeare among the ruins. The story moves between before the outbreak, during it, and years later. It is less violent than a typical end-of-the-world show. It is more interested in art, memory, and the ties between people.

stranger-things.plot: In an Indiana town in the 1980s, a boy disappears. His friends go looking for him with flashlights and the vocabulary of a tabletop game. An experiment, a world on the other side, and a girl numbered Eleven are connected.
stranger-things.hook: A boy disappears in an American town in the 1980s. His friends and a girl with powers go looking for him. It is full of the retro atmosphere of E.T., Stephen King, and Dungeons & Dragons. The first season is the most complete. The later seasons are bigger. It is easy to watch as a family.

succession.plot: After the media magnate Logan Roy has a stroke, his four children start calculating who can take the company. They have money and they have injuries, and they have a sentence they can never say: their father does not intend to give it to anyone.
succession.hook: A media empire’s father and his four children fight over the succession. It is a lot like a modern King Lear. The dialogue is cruel and funny. Almost everyone is awful, and good to watch. Four seasons, a complete shape, a clean ending. It won the Emmy for best drama three times.

survivor.plot: A group of strangers is put in a remote place, lives in teams, wins competitions, and votes people out at tribal council. The last one left takes the money. Physical strength soon matters less than alliances.
survivor.hook: One of the originals of reality television: a group of people is dropped on a deserted island, competes in tribes, votes each other out, and the last person wins a million dollars. What actually decides it is alliances and betrayal. It has run more than forty seasons and is still on.

ted-lasso.plot: Ted Lasso, an American football coach, is hired to manage an English soccer team. The owner originally expected him to wreck it. He starts by changing the locker room, with biscuits and a refusal to mock people.
ted-lasso.hook: An American football coach who knows nothing about soccer is hired to manage a Premier League team. He is optimistic to the point of seeming foolish, and slowly infects the people around him. The first season is one of the warmest workplace comedies. Later seasons make the episodes longer, and the pace looser.

the-americans.plot: Philip and Elizabeth are KGB agents planted in the Washington suburbs. In public they are a married couple who run a travel agency. In private they carry out Moscow’s assignments. The neighbor next door happens to work for the FBI.
the-americans.hook: During the Cold War, a pair of Soviet spies pose as a married couple in an American suburb. The neighbor who moves in next door is an FBI agent. The missions are tense. What is really good is how the fake marriage becomes a real feeling, and what happens when the children learn the truth. The ending is taken as one of the best closes of a series in recent years.

the-bear.plot: The chef Carmy comes back to Chicago to take over the beef-sandwich shop his brother left when he killed himself. The kitchen is loud and cramped. He wants to make it a real restaurant. The family is still inside the funeral.
the-bear.hook: A top chef comes back to Chicago to take over the sandwich shop his late brother left. The kitchen scenes are extremely tense. The camera and the dialogue feel like a fight. Episode seven of the first season is a single take. “Fishes,” in the second season, is a family Christmas dinner going to pieces.

the-bureau.plot: The undercover officer “Malotru,” of the French external service, comes back to Paris from Damascus and cannot take off an identity he has used for years. The office manages people with forms. People manage themselves with lies.
the-bureau.hook: An undercover series about France’s external intelligence service. There are no James Bond action scenes. The emphasis is on living undercover, interrogation, a false identity, and the psychological pressure. It is filmed very plainly, and is often taken as one of the spy shows closest to real intelligence work. If you like Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, it will suit you.

the-comeback.plot: Valerie Cherish, a sitcom actress past her prime, agrees to film a reality show about her comeback, so her life is filmed a second time. She has to please a younger writer, and keep up, in front of the camera, the appearance of not being finished.
the-comeback.hook: Lisa Kudrow, Phoebe on Friends, plays an actress past her prime who agrees to let a reality show follow her comeback. The jokes come from her straining to please the camera and constantly humiliating herself. It is embarrassing and sad. It ran one season in 2005 and was cancelled, then came back years later.

the-crown.plot: It follows Elizabeth II from her accession to the turn of the century. The royal family here is a household that cannot resign. Prime ministers, spouses, and children all have to negotiate with the office. Three actors take turns as the queen.
the-crown.hook: From Elizabeth II’s accession into the early twenty-first century. Every two seasons the cast changes, and the characters age with it. Episodes are often built around one historical event, such as the Aberfan disaster or Diana’s interview with the BBC. It suits someone who wants modern British history. Claire Foy and Matt Smith, in the first two seasons, are the most praised.

the-diplomat.plot: Kate Wyler, a career diplomat, is suddenly made the American ambassador to Britain, and arrives with a crisis already burning at the embassy door. Her husband Hal is a diplomat too. The same skills are used to help and to make trouble.
the-diplomat.hook: Kate, a career American diplomat, is suddenly appointed ambassador to Britain, and at the same time has to deal with the crisis in her marriage. The international crises move fast and the dialogue is dense. It is like a workplace political thriller. Keri Russell plays the role as both sharp and a mess.

the-good-place.plot: Eleanor wakes up dead and finds she has entered an afterlife assigned by points, and the file has clearly got the wrong person. The neighbors, a class in moral philosophy, and a polite architect keep this handsome neighborhood going.
the-good-place.hook: The heroine dies and is sent by mistake to the Good Place, so she secretly learns how to be good before anyone notices. It explains ethics and philosophy lightly enough to follow. The end of the first season has a large reversal. Better not to have it spoiled.

the-good-wife.plot: The prosecutor Peter Florrick falls over a sex scandal and corruption. Thirteen years later his wife Alicia returns to a law firm. A case comes in every week. The politics of the firm, and her own name, slowly become more important.
the-good-wife.hook: After her husband goes to prison over a scandal, Alicia goes back to a firm as a lawyer. There is a case each episode, but the long-term interest is the politics of the firm, the campaigns, and the marriage. Among legal shows, it is unusual in paying attention to technology, politics, and the media.

the-great-british-baking-show.plot: Amateur bakers in a tent make a signature bake, a technical challenge, and a showstopper. Someone goes home on the weekend. The people who stay keep working dough. The competition is real, and so is the comfort, which is part of the format.
the-great-british-baking-show.hook: Amateur bakers compete in a tent at cakes, bread, and desserts, and one person is sent home each week. What is particular about it is the mildness: the contestants help each other, and the judges do not manufacture conflict on purpose. After watching it you will probably want to bake something.

the-handmaids-tale.plot: In Gilead, after fertility collapses, women who can bear children are made Handmaids and assigned to the households of the powerful. June lives under the name Offred. Remembering what she used to be called becomes a form of resistance.
the-handmaids-tale.hook: Adapted from Atwood’s novel. The United States is replaced by a religious authoritarian regime, and women who can have children are assigned to the houses of senior officials to bear them. The first season is oppressive and exact. It made Hulu the first streaming service to win the Emmy for best drama. The later seasons got longer, and the reception slipped.

the-leftovers.plot: Two percent of the world’s people vanish at once, with no explanation. Three years later, the people in a small town go on living by means of cults, jobs, and silence. The police officer Garvey only wants the day not to split open again.
the-leftovers.hook: Two percent of the people on earth disappear at once. The show does not explain why. It only cares how the people who remain face the loss. The first season is on the oppressive side. The second, after a move to a new town, finds its feet. The third season’s ending is very moving. It suits someone who can take a slow pace and questions left open.

the-night-of.plot: The college student Nasir borrows his father’s taxi late at night and wakes the next day in a strange apartment, with a body beside him. From the police station to the jail, the case starts rewriting him according to its own procedure.
the-night-of.hook: A Pakistani-American college student wakes up and finds the girl beside him stabbed to death. He becomes the prime suspect. The series shows, step by step, how the police, the lawyers, the prison, and the procedure change a person. Adapted from the British series Criminal Justice. Eight episodes.

the-oa.plot: Prairie comes home after years missing. Her sight has returned, and she refuses to explain where she has been. She gathers five people and teaches them a set of movements, which she says may be a way to leave this world.
the-oa.hook: A blind woman missing for seven years comes home. She has her sight back, and she claims she has been to another world. It mixes science fiction, religion, and mysticism, and the style is its own. It was cancelled after two seasons, with the ending stopped on a large unanswered question.

the-office-uk.plot: David Brent, the regional manager of a paper company in Slough, agrees to be filmed for a documentary and understands management as a performance. Tim likes the receptionist Dawn. Almost no one in the office wants to be filmed.
the-office-uk.hook: The original of the American version. Two seasons plus two Christmas specials, fourteen episodes. Ricky Gervais’s boss, David Brent, is embarrassing enough that you want to cover your face. The mockumentary comedy became popular from this. It is colder, more bitter, and shorter than the American version.

the-office-us.plot: At the Scranton branch of a paper company in Pennsylvania, the manager Michael Scott treats the office as his stage. A fake documentary records the sales, the romances, and the parties no one wants to attend.
the-office-us.hook: A mockumentary of daily life at a paper company. Every time the boss, Michael, tries to be a good person, he wrecks it. Jim and Pam’s relationship is the reason a lot of people stay. The first season is still imitating the British original. From the second season it finds its own style. The first seven seasons are the best.

the-pitt.plot: The emergency room of a hospital in Pittsburgh. An episode is about an hour of a shift. The attending, Robbie, takes the interns through the patients who keep coming in. Private matters can only be fitted between two stretchers.
the-pitt.hook: An episode is roughly one hour of a shift in an emergency room, and the season is one fifteen-hour shift. It does not lean on a romance. It leans on a fast, believable sequence of treatment, and on how tired and damaged the staff are. Noah Wyle, from ER, is the lead. In 2025 it won the Emmys for best drama and lead actor.

the-queens-gambit.plot: Beth Harmon, an orphan, sees the chessboard in the tranquilizers at her adoptive home, and then plays her way to international tournaments in the 1960s. The talent is real. So are the dependence, the loneliness, and a world that wants her to look good.
the-queens-gambit.hook: Beth, who grows up in an orphanage, becomes a chess champion on talent, and at the same time fights an addiction to drugs and alcohol. You can follow it without knowing chess. The matches are filmed with the tension of a sports movie. The 1960s clothes and design are beautiful. Seven episodes and it is done.

the-rehearsal.plot: Fielder builds full-scale sets for real people so they can rehearse a difficult conversation first. The plan gets more complete, until his own life is put into the rehearsal.
the-rehearsal.hook: Nathan Fielder helps ordinary people “rehearse” a crucial moment, such as confessing a lie to a friend, and will build a one-to-one copy of a bar to do it. As the show goes on it gets out of control, and he himself is pulled in. Funny, eerie, and unsettling.

the-shield.plot: Vic Mackey leads a strike team in Los Angeles’s Farmington district and buys results on the street with illegal methods. A murder in the pilot is not forgotten. For the next seven years it keeps collecting interest from him.
the-shield.hook: The Los Angeles cop Vic Mackey and his team answer violence with violence and skim drug money. At the end of the pilot he kills a colleague with his own hands. The whole series is a rope slowly tightening, to see whether he can get out from under what he owes. The ending is widely taken as one of the best endings in television.

the-thick-of-it.plot: The ministers of a British government department have not decided the policy yet, and the communications chief Malcolm Tucker has already burst in to rewrite the draft, swear, and clean up the mess. The wording of one sentence can ruin a morning.
the-thick-of-it.hook: A political satire about a British government department. The ministers are exhausted by the press and by policy disasters. Peter Capaldi’s communications chief, Malcolm Tucker, is famous for the inventiveness of his swearing. The creator later took the style to the United States for Veep, and also made the film In the Loop.

the-white-lotus.plot: Each season moves to another White Lotus hotel. The opening tells you someone will die this week, and then goes back to watch how the guests treat the staff, the local people, and each other as part of the holiday.
the-white-lotus.hook: Each season changes the luxury resort and the batch of rich guests. It tells you at the start that someone has died, then goes back over the week. It satirizes the arrogance and the emptiness of the rich, and it also films the position of the staff. The first season is in Hawaii, the second in Sicily, the third in Thailand. The seasons can be watched on their own.

the-wire.plot: A narcotics unit in Baltimore sets its sights on the dealer Stringer Bell and on Omar. Five seasons pass through the street, the docks, city hall, the schools, and the newspaper. The police are only one line in the city.
the-wire.hook: It is not a cop show that closes a case each week. Five seasons cover the drug corners, the dockworkers’ union, a city election, the public schools, and a newspaper. Put together, they are how a whole city fails. The creator, Simon, was a reporter in Baltimore, and a lot of the detail comes from real cases. There are many people at the start, and a lot of slang. Get through the first three or four episodes and it takes hold.

true-detective.plot: The Louisiana detectives Hart and Cohle tell the same murder from 1995 and from 2012. A girl’s body takes them into the swamp, a church, and an old case they do not want closed.
true-detective.hook: Watch the first season. Two detectives recall a murder with the color of a cult, on two timelines. Matthew McConaughey’s pessimistic philosophical lines are famous. The long take of about six minutes at the end of episode four has been discussed over and over. The Southern swamp, the churches, and the factories give it a strong gothic atmosphere.

twin-peaks-the-return.plot: Twenty-five years after the Laura Palmer case, Agent Cooper has to get back to Twin Peaks, and he does not come back whole. Across eighteen episodes there is an atomic bomb, a house by the road, and a stretch of waiting in which almost nothing moves.
twin-peaks-the-return.hook: David Lynch’s continuation, made 25 years after the original. Eighteen episodes. Do not expect an ordinary sequel. It is close to an eighteen-hour experimental film. The atomic-bomb passage in episode eight is especially astonishing. People who like Lynch will be absorbed.

veep.plot: Selina Meyer is the vice president of the United States. The schedule is full of visits no one wants and alliances that can collapse at any moment. She wants to be president. The staff want to survive. Each episode’s crisis comes from the previous offhand sentence.
veep.hook: The vice president and her staff are always putting out fires. Politics here is only passing the blame, grabbing the camera, and swearing. The obscenities are extremely inventive, and the pace is fast enough that you will pause and go back. Julia Louis-Dreyfus won six Emmys for lead actress in a comedy for it.

watchmen.plot: It is not a panel-by-panel remake of the comic. The story opens with the 1921 massacre in Tulsa and then settles in an America where masked police are still on duty. Angela, played by Regina King, has to find out the identity her father’s generation left her.
watchmen.hook: It is not a remake of the film. It is a sequel to the original comic, set in 2019. It joins a superhero story to the history of racial violence in the United States. It opens with the 1921 Tulsa massacre. You can watch it without the comic. If you have read it, there is more. It won 11 Emmys.
